Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting
October 20, 2020 at 6:30pm
Veterans Park Community Center
508 North Lincoln, Cabot, Arkansas 72023

I.

Call to Order/Roll Call
Maggie Cope called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
Present: Maggie Cope, Greg Sled, Nick Whitaker, Sheila DeArmond

II.

Minutes of Regular Meeting
Minutes from the meeting held on September 15, 2020 were presented. GREG SLED
MOTIONED TO ACCEPT THE MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 15, 2020, SECOND BY NICK WHITAKER
TRICIA AMBEAU. ALL SAY AYE.

III.

Financials
General Director Travis presented the September 2020 financials. NICK WHITAKER MOTIONED
TO ACCEPT THE SEPTEMBER 2020 FINACIALS AS PRESENTED, SECOND BY GREG SLED. Mr.
Young reported that the department is not out of the woods yet but doing better overall with
revenue loss due to Covid 19. ALL SAY AYE IN PASSING THE AUGUST 2020 FINANCIALS.

IV.

Programs
Program Director Lorenzo Mendoza reported that the parks have two weeks left playing
baseball and softball. Soccer and volleyball will end soon. Registration for youth wrestling has
begun and youth basketball registration will begin this Thursday. Basketball regular season will
begin January 4th if all goes according to plan. The associations have been billed for their gate
fees at $15.00 per player.
Cabot Youth Football reported that their numbers are good, and all is going well. They have
one team playing in the league from out of town.
Cabot Youth Cheer reported that the group has 50 girls, which is about 1/3 of last season and
all is going well.
Cabot Panther Flag Football has been playing for 3 weeks now with 135 players registered and
all is going well. Nick Whitaker asked that the group address parking issues at Cabot Junior High
South.

113

--- page 119 (text layer) ---
BMX is rolling right along averaging 28 riders and about to end their season. The track is in real
good shape and the building is ready to be closed in.

V.

Construction/Directors Report
General Director Travis Young provides update. An Eagle Scout has requested to complete a
project for the parks by building and installing structures to hang hammocks on. The City of
Cabot will assist with erosion issues at the Community Pond. Rye grass has been planted where
needed. The 2019 RR Grant has been completed and we should be receiving some funds left
from the project. The 2020 Grant presentation is coming soon. USA Swim will be holding a
meet at the center, which will produce some revenue with a per swimmer charge. The 2021
budget processes are beginning and due to Covid 19 there will be some challenges.

VI.

Old Business
None

VII.

New Business
Jeff Green presented the finding of the 2019 audit. Mr. Green reported a clean audit with no
issues and overall ended the year with $35,000.00.
Aquatic Park Repairs- There are some issues with the sun damaging the slides and other
structures that need repair. Mr. Young will ask A&P to assist with funds needed. NICK
WHITAKER MOTIONED TO TABLE THE DISCUSSION UNTIL MR. YOUNG MEETS WITH A&P,
SECOND BY GREG SLED. ALL SAY AYE.
2020/2021 Basketball Season –Mr. Mendoza asked the commission their opinions on collecting
gate and how to form teams. He reported that a survey was given to last year’s participants on
whether they would like to draft as in previous years or form teams based on the schools the
players attend. Results of the survey were 53% said yes to drafting teams and 47% said assign
schools. Discussion lead to what is best for the community. The commission has no issues with
collection gate fees up front and charge an extra $20.00 per player during registration. One
plus is not having teenagers sitting at the gate with money bags.

Cabot City Council Work Session
Veterans Park Event Center
November 2, 2020
6:30 p.m.

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on social
distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot moved the monthly
Work Session to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508 N. Lincoln, as advertised. This
allowed for spacing between chairs, as suggested. The event was successfully streamed
through YouTube. You may view this meeting at (Part 1) - https://youtu.be/K-Y ZaarjO-

E (Part 2) - https://youtu.be/vPJ3UAo03dww.

Council members present were: Ed Long, Kevin Davis, Norma Naquin, Matt Webber,
Damon Bivins, James Reid and Ron Waymack. Others present: Mayor Ken Kincade,
City Attorney Ben Hooper, City Paralegal Jessica Looper, City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy
Yocom, and Matthew Hood, Human Resources Director.

Mayor Kincade opened the meeting at 6:30 p.m.

Municipal Services Committee Business: (Members are: Long, Reid & Webber)

As Chairman, Ed Long opened with a discussion on the workers compensation
contract. Matthew Hood, Human Resources Director, explained the insurance was bid out
and only one company submitted a bid. Motion to place this item on this month’s Council
Meeting Agenda by James, second by Damon. Motion passed unanimously by the
committee members.

As discussed during the Public Input Section of the October 19" Council Meeting, the

ordinance regarding requirements for a parking pad other than a driveway was discussed
again. Mayor Kincade reaffirmed he would not enforce the ordinance until a solution
could be determined. Norma Naquin announced she requested to repeal Ordinance No.
30 of 2020 so that the requirements for parking RV's, boats, trailers, etc. could be
explored further and legislated differently. But City Attorney Ben Hooper advised her to
only repeal the sections regarding this issue, which are, Section 2 and 3. It was explained
that rewriting these sections will take time. It will need to go before the Planning
Commission for a Public Hearing and the outcome of those meeting (s) will be sent back
to the Council for adoption into the Code of Cabot. At least sixteen homeowners
addressed the Council. All were in opposition of the current requirements of the Code of
Cabot regarding a hard surface for parking in an area other than the driveway. This topic
was discussed from 6:35 p.m. to 8:04 p.m.
Budget & Personnel Committee Business: (Members are: Webber & Naquin) Matt
Webber announced he will fill in as Chairman of this committee due to the vacancy on
the Council and James Reid will be added as a committee member. He also asked the
committee to join him in a meeting following the Council Meeting on the 16™ to discuss
the 2021 budget.

No action.

Police & Fire Committee Business: (Members are: Bivins, Waymack and Long)

Nothing on agenda. No action.

The meeting ended at 8:16 p.m. with a motion to adjourn by Ed, second by Matt and a
unanimous vote.

Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting
October 20, 2020 at 6:30pm
Veterans Park Community Center
508 North Lincoln, Cabot, Arkansas 72023

I.

Call to Order/Roll Call
Maggie Cope called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
Present: Maggie Cope, Greg Sled, Nick Whitaker, Sheila DeArmond

II.

Minutes of Regular Meeting
Minutes from the meeting held on September 15, 2020 were presented. GREG SLED
MOTIONED TO ACCEPT THE MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 15, 2020, SECOND BY NICK WHITAKER
TRICIA AMBEAU. ALL SAY AYE.

III.

Financials
General Director Travis presented the September 2020 financials. NICK WHITAKER MOTIONED
TO ACCEPT THE SEPTEMBER 2020 FINACIALS AS PRESENTED, SECOND BY GREG SLED. Mr.
Young reported that the department is not out of the woods yet but doing better overall with
revenue loss due to Covid 19. ALL SAY AYE IN PASSING THE AUGUST 2020 FINANCIALS.

IV.

Programs
Program Director Lorenzo Mendoza reported that the parks have two weeks left playing
baseball and softball. Soccer and volleyball will end soon. Registration for youth wrestling has
begun and youth basketball registration will begin this Thursday. Basketball regular season will
begin January 4th if all goes according to plan. The associations have been billed for their gate
fees at $15.00 per player.
Cabot Youth Football reported that their numbers are good, and all is going well. They have
one team playing in the league from out of town.
Cabot Youth Cheer reported that the group has 50 girls, which is about 1/3 of last season and
all is going well.
Cabot Panther Flag Football has been playing for 3 weeks now with 135 players registered and
all is going well. Nick Whitaker asked that the group address parking issues at Cabot Junior High
South.

113

BMX is rolling right along averaging 28 riders and about to end their season. The track is in real
good shape and the building is ready to be closed in.

V.

Construction/Directors Report
General Director Travis Young provides update. An Eagle Scout has requested to complete a
project for the parks by building and installing structures to hang hammocks on. The City of
Cabot will assist with erosion issues at the Community Pond. Rye grass has been planted where
needed. The 2019 RR Grant has been completed and we should be receiving some funds left
from the project. The 2020 Grant presentation is coming soon. USA Swim will be holding a
meet at the center, which will produce some revenue with a per swimmer charge. The 2021
budget processes are beginning and due to Covid 19 there will be some challenges.

VI.

Old Business
None

VII.

New Business
Jeff Green presented the finding of the 2019 audit. Mr. Green reported a clean audit with no
issues and overall ended the year with $35,000.00.
Aquatic Park Repairs- There are some issues with the sun damaging the slides and other
structures that need repair. Mr. Young will ask A&P to assist with funds needed. NICK
WHITAKER MOTIONED TO TABLE THE DISCUSSION UNTIL MR. YOUNG MEETS WITH A&P,
SECOND BY GREG SLED. ALL SAY AYE.
2020/2021 Basketball Season –Mr. Mendoza asked the commission their opinions on collecting
gate and how to form teams. He reported that a survey was given to last year’s participants on
whether they would like to draft as in previous years or form teams based on the schools the
players attend. Results of the survey were 53% said yes to drafting teams and 47% said assign
schools. Discussion lead to what is best for the community. The commission has no issues with
collection gate fees up front and charge an extra $20.00 per player during registration. One
plus is not having teenagers sitting at the gate with money bags.

IX.

Adjournment
The next meeting will be held on November 17, 2020. GREG SLED MOTIONED TO ADJOURN AT
7:03PM, SECOND BY SHEILA DEARMOND. ALL SAY AYE.

AGENDA ITEMS
In response to the 2020 COVID-19 outbreak and restrictions placed on

conferencing tool Zoom.

Planning Commission at 7:00 PM, in the Veterans Park Event Center.

led by Chairman Young.

A roll call was conducted. The following persons were present:
Commission members Liz Bird, Chuck Prater, Matt Moudy, Mitch Ward
Ronny Loe, Chairman Young and City Attorney Ben Hooper. Garver –
City Planner Kevin Gambrill and Mayor Ken Kincade were present via
Zoom. Absent was Claude Irvin.

meeting were approved with a motion by Mr. Loe and a second by Mr.
Prater, Motion passed unanimously by a Roll Call Vote.

a) Rezone from R-1 to C-2 – undeveloped North Polk Street (Angie
Horn)

b) Rezone from R-1 to R-4M – 801 and 904 Eagle Street (formerly
Mocking bird Lane) (Lemons Engineering)
Chairman Young recused himself. Vice Chairman Prater led
discussion. After a brief discussion about street improvements a
Motion to adopt by Ms. Bird, second by Mr. Loe, Motion passed
unanimously by a Roll Call Vote, 5-0-0.

access to highway 321, a Motion to table by Mr. Loe, second by Mr.
Moudy, motion to table passed unanimously by Roll Call Vote, 5-0-0.
b. 403 Commerce Park (Mark Allen)
After a brief discussion a Motion by Mr. Ward, second by Mr. Moudy,
to allow Mr. Allen to conduct a recreational sporting center in an I-1
District until zoning can be amended in the UDC. Motion passed
unanimously by Roll Call Vote, 5-0-0.

d. Adjournment

Council Meeting Minutes
November 16, 2020

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on
social distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot
moved the monthly Council Meeting to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508
N. Lincoln, as advertised. This allowed for spacing between chairs, as
suggested. The event was successfully streamed through YouTube. You

may view this meeting at https://youtu.be/-PDr-6NQFO0s.

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular meeting of the Cabot City
Council at 7:00 p.m. on November 16, 2020 in the Veterans Park Event
Center. Council Member Matt Webber led the prayer and Council Member
Ed Long led the Pledge of Allegiance.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present:
Ronald Waymack, James Reid, Matt Webber, Damon Bivins, Ed Long, and
Kevin Davis. Norma Naquin was absent. Also in attendance were City
Attorney Ben Hooper, City Paralegal Jessica Looper, City Clerk & Treasurer
Tammy Yocom, IT Director Roger Self and HR Director Matthew Hood.

by Mr. Davis and second by Mr. Reid. Motion passed unanimously by a Roll
Call Vote.

The minutes of the October 5th Special Council Meeting were approved with
a motion by Mr. Davis and second by Mr. Reid. Motion passed unanimously
by a Roll Call Vote.

Motion to read legislation by title only by Mr. Davis, second by Mr. Webber.
Motion passed unanimously by a Roll Call Vote.

Jurisdiction Trail.

ARKANSAS THAT:

to Ward Multi-Jurisdiction Trail in the amount of $250,000.00 which is attached hereto as

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

Halff Associates, Inc. (“Halff”) will perform professional design services for the
City of Cabot for developing construction documents for bidding a nearly 6 mile
trail from Cabot City Hall to Ward City Hall. The project will follow the Multi-
Jurisdiction Trail preliminary plans prepared in September 2020. The plans will
include construction budget estimates for the project. Design includes trail design
at storm water crossings.

SCOPE OF SERVICES

A. BASE MAP PREPARATION, AND SITE EVALUATION

1.

Halff will prepare a topographic survey to include, lot lines, right-
of-way, contours, utilities, and all existing above ground elements.
Property owners will be identified should ROW be needed.

B. DEVELOPMENT OF 60% PLANS

1.

Halff will develop 60% plans using the topo graphic survey to
included proposed trail route, associated storm drainage
adjustments, light pole locations, erosion control plans,
maintenance of traffic, pedestrian crosswalks, and amenities.
Wetland delineation will be included in this phase to identify any
wetland areas or crossings on the trail that could require
mitigation.

Hydrologic and hydraulic design will be completed to determine
the stormwater flows at stormwater crossings to determine
structure size. Structural analysis for drainage crossing will also
be included for the drainage structure between Austin and Ward
(a tributary of Fourmile Creek).

The 60% plan set will include the site plans, standard details,
preliminary layout of drainage structures and ROW deeds.

Halff will provide plans for city review following the 60% submittal
to ARDOT and Metroplan.

A\cost estimate will be prepared based on the 60% plan set using
ARDOT weighted averages.

Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting
November 17, 2020 at 6:30pm
Veterans Park Community Center
508 North Lincoln, Cabot, Arkansas 72023

I.

Call to Order/Roll Call
Maggie Cope called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
Present: Maggie Cope, Greg Sled, Nick Whitaker, Sheila DeArmond, John C. Thompson, John
Rudd.

II.

Minutes of Regular Meeting
Minutes from the meeting held on October 20, 2020 were presented. GREG SLED MOTIONED
TO ACCEPT THE MINUTES OF OCTOBER 15, 2020, SECOND BY JOHN C. THOMPSON, ALL SAY
AYE.

III.

Financials
General Director Travis Young presented the October 2020 financials. GREG SLED MOTIONED
TO ACCEPT THE OCTOBER 2020 FINANCIALS AS PRESENTED, SECOND BY JOHN C. THOMPSON.
Mr. Young reported the basketball income came in later than usual and the janitorial supplies
are higher than normal. With all going on right now the department is where it should be
financially at this time. ALL SAY AYE IN PASSING THE OCTOBER 2020 FINANCIALS.

IV.

Programs
Program Director Lorenzo Mendoza reported that fall sports have ended except for a few
games left with football and cheer. Letters were sent to all those who participated in fall sports
thanking them for their support. Basketball registration is currently being held with about 40
less registered at the same time last year. Wrestling registration is also being held at this time.
Swim meets are being held with no spectators permitted.
Cabot Youth Football reported all went well with the season.
BMX is coming to the end of their season and will focus on raising funds to finish their building.
Cabot Youth Cheer reported all is going well with their season.
Panther Flag Football had 135 players and had little issues this season.

V.

Construction/Directors Report
General Director Travis Young reported that the maintenance crew is working to get the
facilities winterized. There are some erosion problems within the parks that are being

124

addressed. LED lighting is being installed at the outdoor parks. An Eagle Scout is working on a
hammock project for the outdoors, which is very trendy currently. The Event Center will add a
new pipe and drape system for events. The Cabot Chamber of Commerce has donated several
carts to help with events. Fitness classes are picking up and classes are filling quickly.
Participants may call 24 hours in advance to register for classes. The maintenance crew is also
overseeding fields. Several job opens will be filled soon. The department will move forward
with the bike trails in 2021. Lorenzo Mendoza stated he would like to have something to give
back to the coaches that volunteer their time and is looking for sponsors to help with some
type of thank you gift.
VI.

Old Business
Pool Repairs. A&P has agreed to fund both repair projects at the Water Park. The repairs will
begin in the Spring and Mr. Young asked the commission if they preferred using the
Government programs or bid out the work. Several companies were discussed, and the
decision was made to put the projects out for bid.

VII.

New Business
American Legion Baseball was present and gave updates for the Richie Road Babe Ruth Field.
They are working with Baseball of Tomorrow with Major League Baseball. The grant will not
cover all items, but they are working with several sponsors and donations to complete the
project. Roofing, fencing, and ½ off labor have be offered. The group would like to put up
sponsor signs on the outfield fencing once the project is completed. They are seeking approval
from the commission to keep moving forward. Mr. Young will get with Parks Attorney Greg
Crumpton to draw up an agreement. JOHN C. THOMPSON MOTIONED TO DRAW UP AN
AGREEMENT, WITH ASSISTANCE FROM ATTORNEY GREG CRUMPTON, TO ALLOW CABOT
AMERICAN LEGION BASEBALL TO MOVE FORWARD WITH FIELD RENOVATIONS ON THE RICHIE
ROAD BALL FIELD, SECOND BY GREG SLED, ALL SAY AYE.
Fireworks 2021 – Staff is asking the commission to set the date of 2021 July 4th celebration.
JOHN RUDD MOTIONED TO HOLD THE 2021 JULY 4TH CELEBRATION ON JULY 4TH, SECOND BY
JOHN C. THOMPSON, ALL SAY AYE.
Worker Comp. Policy – tabled until later date.
Maggie Cope had to exit the meeting; John C. Thompson resumed meeting as Chairman.

125

Budget 2021 Update – The budget cannot be finalized until the City of Cabot and Cabot A&P
finalize their current budgets. Commission gave Mr. Young approval to send an email to the
City to see what help will be made available.
Bond Projects - The City of Cabot is thinking about refinancing the 2013 bonds in 2021. In the
event CPR has a chance to add additional facilities a wish list will need to be done. Once a list is
done staff can work on the numbers for facilities. John C. Thompson suggested another
entrance into the Sportsplex. Other items mentioned were a pickleball complex, indoor
swimming complex, adding another inclusive playground with a splash pad. Turfing the
remaining baseball fields, sand volleyball courts, and more soccer fields, etc. Growth of all
sports and recreation was discussed. Mr. Young will do more research on the projects.
VIII.

Community Input
None

IX.

Adjournment
The next meeting will be held on December 15, 2020. JOHN RUDD MOTIONED TO ADJOURN AT
7:22PM, SECOND BY NICK WHITAKER. ALL SAY AYE.

CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS
Council Meeting Minutes
December 14, 2020

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on
social distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot
moved the monthly Council Meeting to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508
N. Lincoln, as advertised. This allowed for spacing between chairs, as
suggested. The event was successfully streamed through YouTube. You
may view this meeting at https://youtu.be/tiatlw-pEXM.

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular meeting of the Cabot City
Council at 7:00 p.m. on December 14, 2020 in the Veterans Park Event
Center. Council Member Kevin Davis led the prayer and Council Member
Damon Bivins led the Pledge of Allegiance.

it Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present:
Ronald Waymack, James Reid, Matt Webber, Damon Bivins, Ed Long,
Norma Naquin and Kevin Davis. The City has a vacancy in Ward 2, Position
1 at this time. Also in attendance were City Attorney Ben Hooper, City
Paralegal Jessica Looper, City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom, IT Director
Roger Self and HR Director Matthew Hood.

Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters

With appreciation, Mayor Kincade presented each outgoing Council Member
a plaque detailing their years of service. Those members whose term is up
on December 31, 2020 are: Mr. Kevin Davis, Mr. Damon Bivins and Ms.
Norma Naquin.

The minutes of the October 29" Special Council Meeting and the November
16" Council Meeting were approved with a motion by Ms. Naquin and
second by Mr. Reid. Motion passed unanimously by a Roll Call Vote.

Motion to read legislation by title only by Mr. Long, second by Mr. Reid.
Motion passed unanimously by a Roll Call Vote.
